column2: Fascists support expanding social reforms and eliminating political reforms, and will oppose any reforms if the ruling party is not fascist
Reactionaries always attempt to overturn reforms, reversing both political and social reforms
Conservatives tend to maintain the status quo, but may turn to support reforms when struggle is intense
Socialists want to see new social reform laws, but may turn to support political reforms when struggle is intense
Communists want to enact social reform laws, but want to see political reforms reversed
Liberals want to enact new political reform laws, but will also support social reforms when struggle is intense
Anarcho-liberals want to see social reforms reversed and will not support any new reforms of any kind

With advances in weapon design including breech-loading, mechanization, semi-automatic and other technologies, the industrial output of small arms developed greatly in the 19th century.

The design and production of basic munitions achieved tremendous progress in the 19th century. Advanced weapon design — from muzzle-loading to breech-loading to semi-automatic and machine guns — naturally required corresponding ammunition design and production.

The Victorian era witnessed tremendous progress in humanity's ability to research explosives. At the beginning of the era it was only slightly more advanced than ordinary black powder, but by the end came the birth of plastic explosives and nitroglycerin.

The 19th century Industrial Revolution truly affected all areas of human endeavor, and artillery production was no exception. Bronze cannons that originally required long hours of molding became industrialized and precise in the hands of industrial geniuses like Alfred Krupp or Hiram Maxim.
